title: Reshape the Matrix
summary: Given an m x n matrix mat and two integers r and c, reshape the matrix into a new r x c matrix while preserving the original elements in the same row-traversing order.
statement: Given an m x n matrix mat and two integers r and c, reshape the matrix into a new r x c matrix while preserving the original elements in the same row-traversing order. If the reshaping is not possible, return the original matrix.
constraints: If r*c differs from the input cell count, return the original matrix; otherwise preserve row-traversal order in r rows and c columns.
hints: Only the shape changes; flattened row order does not.
First compare cell counts, then map each flat index to old and new coordinates.
Return original if counts differ; fill output from flat index i.
Both matrices represent the same linear row-major sequence when their total cell counts agree.
editorial: Both matrices represent the same linear row-major sequence when their total cell counts agree.

tests.explanation: Flattening row order gives 1,2,3,4 in one row.
Four cells cannot fill eight positions, so return the original shape.
